key_insight: A single fault-counting Monte Carlo run can estimate all logical sensitivities of a quantum error-correcting code at once, replacing many separate finite-difference sweeps.
engineering_relevance: This gives hardware and QEC engineers a much cheaper way to identify dominant noise sources, localize weak qubits, and map threshold behavior in multidimensional noise models.
method: Differentiate logical error rate with respect to each physical noise parameter using fault-count information from one simulation data set.
Estimate the full gradient \(\nabla_{\mathbf p} p_L\) simultaneously instead of one parameter at a time.
Use the sensitivities for error-budget analysis, qubit-level diagnostics, effective code-distance inference, and Newton-based threshold tracing.
evidence_signal: In surface-code simulations with circuit-level noise, the estimator matched finite differences while using roughly 10x to 100x fewer shots for the same variance.
watch_item: The approach depends on access to underlying fault configurations, so implementation must be compatible with the simulator or sampling pipeline.
paper_title: Efficient Estimation of Logical Sensitivities Through Fault-Counting
